SRC-306:R004.evidence: T-1881 own patch, final revision (A-020). R004 is satisfied by three separable mechanisms. (1) A ticket-scoped publication PROHIBITION is an INPUT directive field publication=forbidden on the live BOARD row, one-value vocabulary, valid on any section, so it can only ever subtract publication permission and never grant it; declared in REGISTRY.json ticket_states.known_fields, extensions/schemas/board.schema.json, and board_compaction COMPACTION_DISPOSITION as inline, because a prohibition compacted behind a detail_ref would silently read as not forbidden. (2) Enforcement is independent of the generic goal SHIP exception and precedes any network call: release.plan_release resolves the plan ticket set and raises RELEASE_FORBIDDEN after mode resolution and before the first _remote_snapshot git ls-remote; release._plan_crew_release repeats the same gate because plan_release derives a crew or cohort carrier AFTER its own check, so the batch route would otherwise reach the remote unconsulted (this hole was found by this ticket's own REVIEW self-audit and is pinned by BatchPlannerProhibitionTests); and release._preflight_plan re-reads the LIVE board and refuses again at APPLY, deliberately placed before the STATE/BOARD/LOG hash comparisons so a prohibition written between plan and apply is not masked by the generic rebuild-the-plan answer. (3) The release ATTEMPT and its outcome are recorded separately from ticket lifecycle closure in .saipen/kitchen/release_attempts.jsonl, an append-only O_APPEND plus fsync ledger with a closed outcome vocabulary (RELEASED, NO_PUBLISH_MODE, REFUSED_FORBIDDEN, REFUSED_CODE), written at the public invocation boundary -- saipen ship|push, cohort ship, and the intent SHIP action -- never inside execute_release, because five _tree() equality assertions in test_t1746_crew_terminal_outcome assert a refusal writes nothing at the engine API level. A prohibition refusal carries its ticket identity on the exception so D-06's own case leaves a fully named row, and a ledger write failure is reported to the caller without ever upgrading, downgrading or suppressing a release verdict. Lifecycle closure remains available in a no-publish session, so closure and external publication stay separate questions.
SRC-306:R004.text: A ticket-scoped publication prohibition must be enforced independently of the generic goal SHIP exception: the write guard blocks push/tag/release before any network call, and the release attempt plus its outcome is recorded separately from ticket lifecycle closure.
